meta.notice: Pre-release template: every figure on this page comes from synthetic households and placeholder settings. It is not an estimate of the January to March 2027 cap or its effects.
meta.title: Energy price cap, January to March 2027

basis.bills: annualised: a full year at January to March 2027 prices against a full year at October to December 2026 prices
basis.year: support costs and gains: fiscal year (April to March); the model year 2026 is 2026-27
basis.behaviour: static: energy use does not respond to price
basis.support: gross of clawback unless the measure says otherwise

measures.name: Energy price cap, January to March 2027
measures.description: Placeholder. Moves household electricity and gas prices for January to March 2027 from the forecast path in the model to the announced cap, as one percentage change on both fuels. Prices return to the forecast path from April 2027.

measures.name: Larger Household Energy Payment
measures.description: Placeholder. Raises the Household Energy Payment for households in council tax bands A to D in England from £100 to £200 in 2026-27.

measures.name: Household Energy Payment extended to band E
measures.description: Placeholder. Pays the £100 Household Energy Payment to households in council tax bands A to E in England.

measures.name: Household Energy Payment in Scotland and Wales
measures.description: Placeholder. Pays the £100 to households in bands A to D in Scotland and Wales as well as England. Both devolved governments have been reported as planning this; neither official source is confirmed yet. Band valuations differ by nation.

measures.name: Larger Warm Home Discount
measures.description: Placeholder. Raises the Warm Home Discount from £150 to £300 for the 2026-27 scheme year (England and Wales).

measures.name: Warm Home Discount for disability benefit recipients
measures.description: Placeholder. Adds Personal Independence Payment and Attendance Allowance to the benefits that qualify for the Warm Home Discount.

measures.name: 0% VAT on domestic electricity to March 2028
measures.description: Placeholder. Keeps the 0% VAT rate on domestic electricity in Great Britain from 1 July 2027, when it is due to return to 5%, to 31 March 2028.

measures.name: 0% VAT on domestic gas
measures.description: Placeholder. Cuts VAT on domestic gas from 5% to 0%.
measures.reason: The model has no VAT rate for gas alone: gas shares the reduced rate with other goods, so cutting it would cut theirs too (issue #6).

measures.name: Credit on every household energy bill
measures.description: Placeholder. A £150 credit to every household with an electricity account in 2026-27.

measures.name: Larger Winter Fuel Payment
measures.description: Placeholder. Adds £100 a household to the Winter Fuel Payment for 2026-27: £300 to £400 for the higher rate and £200 to £300 for the lower, with each shared rate (two eligible people in one household) raised by £50. Scotland pays its own Pension Age Winter Heating Payment instead, which this lever does not change.

measures.name: Targeted energy discount
measures.description: Placeholder. A discount of £175 a year for households whose highest individual income is below £24,000 or who receive a means-tested benefit.
measures.reason: The model has no rule for this discount yet: it exists in an earlier PolicyEngine analysis and must be added and checked before it can be estimated.

measures.name: Gas standing charge moved into the unit rate
measures.description: Placeholder. Removes the gas standing charge and recovers the cost through a higher unit rate, so that bills raise the same total.
measures.reason: Computable from the data but not yet computed here: the Microcosm file holds annual household gas kWh (calendar 2024), and gas kWh above zero identifies gas households (24.3m on build 6f918b81), so the shift can be costed as a household rule (issue #4).

measures.name: Part of the electricity standing charge moved into the unit rate
measures.description: Placeholder. Moves half of the electricity standing charge into the unit rate.
measures.reason: The data hold annual electricity kWh but not tariff type, so Economy 7 homes cannot be told apart and a change to the standing charge cannot be estimated (issue #4).

measures.name: Bills held at a set typical level
measures.description: Placeholder. A subsidy per unit that holds the typical Direct Debit bill at £1,723 for January to March 2027.
measures.reason: The model's record of past cap levels changes how it measures typical use in July 2026, so a subsidy based on it would be about 11% out (issue #3).

measures.name: Remaining policy costs moved off electricity bills
measures.description: Placeholder. Moves the remaining Renewables Obligation and Feed-in Tariff costs from electricity bills into taxation.
measures.reason: The model moves electricity and gas prices together, so a change to electricity bills alone cannot be estimated (issue #2).

measures.name: Larger Cold Weather Payment
measures.description: Placeholder. Raises the payment from £25 to £50 a week.
measures.reason: The model does not include the Cold Weather Payment (issue #8).

measures.name: Energy debt relief
measures.description: Placeholder. One-off relief for households with energy debt on means-tested or disability benefits.
measures.reason: The data do not record energy debt, so the official figure is recorded, not estimated.

measures.name: Prepayment levelisation
measures.description: Placeholder. Changes to how prepayment and Direct Debit costs are levelled.
measures.reason: The data show which homes use prepayment meters, but the model has no prices by payment method (issue #4).
